chip-blocks.title: Inside the ADS7952
chip-blocks.alt: Block diagram of the ADS7952: its function blocks, how they connect and which package pins reach each block.
chip-blocks.description: The ADS7952's function blocks inside its outline. Arrows between blocks carry signals or data in the direction they point (both ways where they have two heads). The package pins stand on the left and right edges with their numbers, each wired to the block it reaches.

chip-capabilities.title: What the ADS7952 does
chip-capabilities.alt: Capability map of the ADS7952: Manual mode (supported): Converts the channel each frame names; the result comes two frames later, tagged with its channel; Auto-1 sequence (supported): Scans a programmed list of channels in ascending order, one per frame; Auto-2 sequence (supported): Scans from channel 0 up to a programmed last channel, one per frame; Input range (supported): Selects 0 to VREF or 0 to 2 x VREF, and converts codes to microvolts; Alarm thresholds (supported): A high and a low threshold per channel, signalled on GPIO0 and GPIO1; GPIOs (supported): Four pins on TSSOP, one on VQFN, each an input or an output, read and written with the frames; Power-down (supported): Powers the chip down at the end of a frame, by command or by the GPIO3 input; Reset and checks (supported): Resets every register by command, waits the power-up time and checks that the chip answers.
chip-capabilities.description: Each card is one function of the ADS7952: an icon, its name and what it does for the application. The filled pill says how this driver covers it (legend below); the outlined pills are the chip registers behind it. The coverage table in the README gives the driver calls and the datasheet section of each card.

chip-circuit-typical.title: ADS7952: Typical application
chip-circuit-typical.alt: Schematic of the ADS7952 typical application: the chip with U2 MCU, U3 REF5025, C1 capacitor 10 µF, C2 capacitor 1 µF, C3 capacitor 1 µF, C4 capacitor 150 pF, C5 capacitor 150 pF; the MCU wires carry the port hooks Transfer().
chip-circuit-typical.description: A schematic. The MCU is on the left, each of its pins level with the chip pin it connects to; above each wire is the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it. Supply pins point up to their supply and decoupling, ground pins down. Pins on the right carry the loads and the pins tied to a supply or ground; a cross marks a pin left open. A dot is a junction; wires that cross without a dot are not connected.

chip-frame-spi.title: ADS7952: SPI frame
chip-frame-spi.alt: SPI frame of the ADS7952, 16 bits, most significant bit first. Manual: mode (bits 15 to 12), program (bit 11), channel (bits 10 to 7), range (bit 6), power down (bit 5), GPIO read (bit 4), GPIO data (bits 3 to 0); Reply: channel address (bits 15 to 12), 12-bit result (bits 11 to 0). Below, the SPI mode 0 waveform of one transfer in the same bit grid.
chip-frame-spi.description: One SPI frame of the ADS7952, 16 bits in a row from the most significant (left, sent first) to the least significant (right). Each row is one kind of frame; each coloured box a field, with its first and last bit number under it. The waveform below draws the select, the clock and the data lines over the same bits.

chip-hero.title: ADS7952
chip-hero.alt: Overview of the ADS7952, a 12-channel, 12-bit SAR analog-to-digital converter that samples one single-ended input per 16-bit SPI frame at up to 1 MSPS, in a manual order or in one of two automatic sequences. A MCU talks to it over SPI; it drives GPIO0 to GPIO3; it reads back Analog inputs, External reference. Headline figures: 12 x 12-bit single-ended inputs, one ADC; 1 MSPS sample rate; 20 MHz SPI clock, one 16-bit frame per sample; 2.7 to 5.25 V analog supply; I/O 1.7 to 5.25 V; 0 to 2 x VREF input range, or 0 to VREF; 1 µA power-down current.
chip-hero.description: The ADS7952 in the middle, drawn as its TSSOP-38 package. On the left the MCU that runs the driver, joined to it by SPI. To the right, what the chip drives, in the order the power flows. Below it, what the chip reads back. The tiles at the bottom are the headline numbers, each with the datasheet section and page it comes from.

chip-pinout.title: ADS7952 pinout, TSSOP-38
chip-pinout.alt: Pinout of the ADS7952 in TSSOP-38, top view: 38 pins, each with its name, its electrical type as a colour and the driver hook that uses it.
chip-pinout.description: The ADS7952 seen from the top, in its TSSOP-38 package. Pin 1 is marked by the dot; the numbers run counter-clockwise from it. Each pad is coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Next to it is the pin's name and, in mono, the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it; a pin without a hook is not used by the driver.

chip-wiring-typical.title: Wiring: Typical application
chip-wiring-typical.alt: Wiring of the ADS7952 for the Typical application: MCU SPI SCK to SCLK (Transfer()); MCU SPI MOSI to SDI (Transfer()); MCU SPI MISO to SDO (Transfer()); MCU GPIO / CS to CS (Transfer()); REFP to REF5025 OUT. Supplies, grounds and the support parts are listed under the drawing.
chip-wiring-typical.description: The MCU on the left, the ADS7952 in the middle, the blocks it drives on the right. Each wire is coloured by the chip pin's electrical type and carries the net name and the chip pin number above it and, under it, the driver hook that uses it (and any part on the net). The boxes underneath list the supplies, the support parts and the pins this circuit leaves unconnected.

driver-layers.title: The layers, one of them yours
driver-layers.alt: Layer diagram: your application calls the ADS7952 core, which sends register reads and writes through the SPI port contract to the port class you write, which drives the chip; the core and the contract are the same on every MCU.
driver-layers.description: Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers.

frame-pipeline.title: A result comes back two frames after its channel
frame-pipeline.alt: Two timing grids of 16-bit frames. Manual: a Manual word selects channel 4 in frame N, the multiplexer acquires it in frame N + 1 and its result comes back in frame N + 2. Auto-1: the Auto-1 word restarts the sequence 2, 5, 6 in frame N, and from frame N + 2 on every Auto-1 word returns the next channel.
frame-pipeline.description: Each column is one 16-bit frame, CS low for 16 SCLK cycles, left to right in time. In each panel the top row is the word the driver sends on SDI, the middle row the channel the multiplexer acquires during that frame, and the bottom row the reply on SDO: the conversion of the channel acquired in the frame before, sampled at this frame's CS falling edge, tagged with its address in DO15:12. In Manual mode (top) ReadChannel(4) selects channel 4 with a Manual word, sends a "continue" word and then the Manual word for channel 4 again (it carries the range once more), and keeps the third reply, whose address must be 4; the two replies before it still belong to the previous channel. In Auto-1 (bottom), entering the mode restarts the sequence at its first channel: with channels 2, 5 and 6 programmed, the first result arrives two frames after the Auto-1 word, and from then on every Auto-1 word without restart (DI11 = 1, the range again) returns the next channel of the sequence, so a pass costs one frame per channel. The timing is the datasheet's Figures 51 and 53; the frame counts come from ReadChannel(), readSelected(), scan() and collect() in src/ads7952.ipp.

one-read-through-the-layers.title: One read through the layers
one-read-through-the-layers.alt: A channel read through the layers: the first ReadChannel sends a select word and two continue words through your port to get the result, and a repeat read of the same channel needs one continue word.
one-read-through-the-layers.description: Participants, left to right: Your code, ADS7952<Port> and Your port. The steps run from top to bottom. Your code sends ReadChannel(4) to ADS7952<Port>. ADS7952<Port> sends Transfer(0x1A00: Manual, DI11, channel 4) to Your port. Your port returns true, reply of an earlier channel to ADS7952<Port>. ADS7952<Port> sends Transfer(0x0000: continue) to Your port. Your port returns true, reply acquired before the select to ADS7952<Port>. ADS7952<Port> sends Transfer(0x0000: continue) to Your port. Your port returns true, 0x4xxx: address 4, the result to ADS7952<Port>. ADS7952<Port> returns Result<uint16_t>{code, Ok} to Your code. Your code sends ReadChannel(4) to ADS7952<Port>. ADS7952<Port> sends Transfer(0x0000: continue) to Your port. Your port returns true, 0x4xxx to ADS7952<Port>. ADS7952<Port> returns Result<uint16_t>{code, Ok} to Your code.
